translations.answer: Within the paper's 51 cm Robotis OP3, external-MoCap, soft-floor, simplified-1v1 ODD, separately training soccer and get-up skills and then combining posture-conditioned adaptive teacher regularization, a pool of opponent snapshots from the first quarter of training, and delay/offset/friction/payload/disturbance randomization around a position-control loop produces a unified hardware policy. In matched get-up-and-shoot trials, hardware scored 29/50 versus 35/50 in simulation, and the five-seed Figure 7 ablation supports the training recipe; the result does not guarantee onboard vision, full-size humanoids, or open human-shared operation.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The robot operates on the reported protected 5 m by 4 m field with reliable external ball, opponent, goal, and robot state.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: A fast robot-specific position-control loop, calibrated joints, charged batteries, soft flooring, and mechanical inspection are available.
translations.applicability.assumptions.2: The result is not generalized beyond the 51 cm, 3.5 kg Robotis OP3 or converted into onboard-vision evidence without a separate validation campaign.
translations.applicability.controllers.0: two-stage Distributional MPO with soccer- and get-up-teacher regularization
translations.applicability.controllers.1: self-play against historical opponents from the first quarter of training
translations.applicability.controllers.2: 40 Hz joint-position-target policy with exponential action filtering and fast PD/PID tracking
translations.applicability.environments.0: simplified 1v1 soccer on a protected 5 m by 4 m field
translations.applicability.environments.1: matched simulated and physical get-up-and-shoot set pieces
translations.applicability.environments.2: isolated walking, turning, recovery, and kicking protocols
translations.applicability.robots.0: Robotis OP3, 51 cm, 3.5 kg, with 20 actuated XM430 joints
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper provides a complete 38-page method and supplement, five-seed multi-opponent ablations, explicit scripted-baseline protocols, and matched 50-simulation/50-hardware set-piece denominators. Confidence is capped because training code is unavailable, several tactical set pieces use about ten trials, the main actor depends on external MoCap game state, and evidence is confined to a small, regularly maintained OP3.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Figures 2, 5, and 7; Table 1; Supplementary Tables S1-S5 and Figures S3-S7
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines the two-stage teacher-to-student pipeline, historical-opponent self-play, state/action interface, randomization and safety shaping, real-behavior protocols, matched 50+50 set-piece transfer, five-seed ablations, compute cost, and the limited vision experiment.
translations.evidence.0.title: Learning Agile Soccer Skills for a Bipedal Robot with Deep Reinforcement Learning
translations.safety.command_limits: Derive robot-specific joint-position, velocity, current/torque, temperature, attitude, and workspace limits; the OP3 values and paper randomization ranges are evidence records, not commands for another platform.
translations.safety.emergency_stop: Test an independent wired or safety-rated stop and a deterministic low-energy response to repeated deadline misses, MoCap/IMU loss, communication timeout, or protective-zone intrusion before dynamic trials.
translations.safety.protective_controls: Use a cleared soft field, bumpers and structural protection appropriate to the platform, fall protection where compatible, remote monitoring, and a safety operator outside the robot and ball envelope.
translations.safety.robot_specific_warning: Published evidence applies to a 51 cm, 3.5 kg OP3 under external MoCap and regular maintenance; adult-size humanoid mass, inertia, fall energy, sensing, and actuator limits are materially different.
translations.safety.staged_deployment: Progress through deterministic simulation, randomized simulation, suspended or low-energy joint checks, isolated recovery/locomotion/kicking, matched set pieces, and only then bounded robot-versus-robot play with explicit stop criteria.
translations.title: How can recovery, walking, turning, kicking, and opponent-aware behavior be trained into one hardware-transferable humanoid policy?
